source: viamin/color_matching solver parity corpus (issue #111). This v1 copy is derived from the documented Elixir WeightedSquaredError semantics and anchored on the WeightedSquaredError doctest case (expected error 0.205) until the canonical corpus lands upstream.
notes: score = sum over conditions with weight > 0 of weight * (candidate - target)^2. A candidate (or target) missing a measurement for any weight > 0 condition is excluded, never treated as zero brightness. Among equal scores the earliest palette candidate wins. See docs/solver-parity-corpus.md for the schema and the refresh procedure.

cases.name: elixir_doctest_anchor
cases.description: The Elixir WeightedSquaredError doctest vector: expected error 0.205 with weights white=0.5 red=1.0 green=1.0 blue=0.0 lps=1.5. Blue is weighted 0 so its values are ignored even though both sides have them; candidate 103 is excluded for lacking green.

cases.name: exact_match_scores_zero
cases.description: Candidates 201 and 203 both score exactly 0.0 (203 carries extra white/blue measurements that are not active); the earliest candidate wins the tie. Extra non-active measurements never change the score.

cases.name: two_way_tie_earliest_candidate_wins
cases.description: Candidates 301 (red 0.4) and 302 (red 0.6) are equidistant from the target red 0.5; both score 0.01 and the earlier palette entry is selected.

cases.name: three_way_tie_earliest_candidate_wins
cases.description: Candidates 401-403 each miss the target by 0.1 on both weighted channels (white weight 2.0, red weight 1.0) and tie at 0.03; the earliest candidate is selected. 404 misses by 0.4 on both channels (0.48).

cases.name: missing_measurement_excludes_never_zero
cases.description: Candidate 501 matches red exactly but has no green measurement: it is excluded. If a missing measurement were wrongly treated as brightness 0, 501 would score 0.01 and win, so the expected selection of 502 (0.04) proves the exclusion policy.

cases.name: zero_weight_channel_not_required
cases.description: Only white is weighted. Candidate 601 measures nothing but white yet is selected: measurements for zero-weight conditions are neither required nor scored.

cases.name: weights_change_winner_white_heavy
cases.description: With weights white=0.5 red=1.0, candidate 701 (misses white entirely) scores 0.5 and beats 702 (misses red entirely) at 1.0.

cases.name: weights_change_winner_red_heavy
cases.description: Same palette and target as weights_change_winner_white_heavy with the weights swapped (white=1.0 red=0.5): the winner flips to 702, proving weights (not candidate order) drive the selection.

cases.name: all_candidates_excluded_no_selection
cases.description: Blue is the only weighted condition and neither candidate measures it: every candidate is excluded and there is no selection.

cases.name: target_missing_required_channel_excludes_all
cases.description: The target itself lacks green (a weight > 0 condition), so every candidate is excluded at the scorer level regardless of its own measurements. No selection exists.

cases.name: five_channel_weighted_mix
cases.description: All five conditions weighted (white 1.0, red 0.25, green 0.5, blue 0.75, lps 1.0). Candidate 1102 trades a small white miss for medium misses elsewhere and wins with 0.0275 over 1101 (0.035) and 1103 (0.25).
